'''Zhang''' '''Xiang''' {{post-nominals|country=HKG|JP}} ({{lang-zh|s=张翔|p=Zhāng Xiáng}}; born December 1963) is a Chinese-American mechanical engineer, currently serving as the 16th [[List of vice-chancellors of the University of Hong Kong|president and vice-chancellor]] of the [[University of Hong Kong]] since July 2018.

Zhang was the inaugural [[Ernest S. Kuh]] Endowed Chaired Professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in the [[United States]], the director of the [[National Science Foundation]] Nano-scale Science and Engineering Center, the director of materials science division, and a senior faculty scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://me.berkeley.edu/people/xiang-zhang/ |title=Professor Xiang Zhang (Brief Biography)|access-date=June 1, 2021}}</ref>

== Education ==
Zhang received a [[Bachelor of Science]] and a [[Master of Science]] from [[Nanjing University]], as well as a Master of Science from the [[University of Minnesota]]. He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from the University of California, Berkeley in 1996.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=President's Office |url=https://presidentoffice.hku.hk/ |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=presidentoffice.hku.hk |archive-date=2023-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208093758/https://presidentoffice.hku.hk/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research results ==
Research mainly focuses on nanoscience and technology, materials physics, photonics and biotechnology. He developed the world's first "metalens" and demonstrated the imaging effect that broke through the diffraction limit of light for the first time. He also invented "plasmon lithography technology" and promoted the development of nanoscale manufacturing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dumé |first=Isabelle |date=2005-04-21 |title=Superlens breakthrough |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/superlens-breakthrough/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Xiang Zhang, JP |url=https://presidentsoffice.hku.hk/leadership/professor-xiang-zhang-jp?lang=zh |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=President's Office |language=zh}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1996 to 1999, he was assistant professor at the [[Pennsylvania State University]] and from 1999 to 2004, associate professor and then full professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], before joining the University of California, Berkeley. Zhang is an elected member of the United States [[National Academy of Engineering]] and of [[Academia Sinica]], a foreign member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], and a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA), [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and [[The International Society for Optical Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://xlab.me.berkeley.edu/ |title=Prof. Xiang Zhang's Laboratory at UC Berkeley|access-date=3 July 2011}}</ref>

Zhang published more than 390 journal papers. His research focuses on materials physics, [[metamaterial]]s and nano-photonics.

On 15 December 2017, the [[University of Hong Kong]] appointed Zhang to the posts of president and vice-chancellor. It was the first time a candidate born and educated to undergraduate degree level in mainland China had been so appointed.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Hong Kong Free Press|date=13 December 2017|title=HKU announces recommendation of Chinese-American scholar Zhang Xiang as school's next vice-chancellor|url=https://www.hongkongfp.com/2017/12/13/hku-announces-recommendation-chinese-american-scholar-zhang-xiang-schools-next-vice-chancellor/|last=Cheung|first=Karen|access-date=13 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Hong Kong Free Press|date=16 December 2017|title=University of Hong Kong appoints Chinese-American scholar Zhang Xiang as vice-chancellor|url=https://www.hongkongfp.com/2017/12/16/university-hong-kong-appoints-chinese-american-scholar-zhang-xiang-vice-chancellor/|last=Cheung|first=Karen|access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref> He assumed office in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web|date=17 July 2018|title=The 16th President and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Hong Kong Professor Xiang Zhang assumes office|url=https://hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/18130.html|access-date=17 July 2018|archive-date=18 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718234629/https://hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/18130.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Events ==
On 3 July 2019, in a statement in response to the [[Storming of the Legislative Council Complex]] two days earlier, Zhang said that he had been "disheartened by the violence" and that he "would like to condemn such acts". In response to a backlash from some 2,000 HKU students, alumni and staff, he stated on 11 July that he opposed violence "by any party, and at any juncture". Zhang agreed to a request by the HKU Student Union to participate in a forum open to students, staff, alumni and the media.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hongkongfp.com/2019/07/14/hku-head-zhang-xiang-promises-dialogue-students-criticism-statement-legco-storming/|title=HKU head Zhang Xiang promises dialogue with students after criticism over statement on LegCo storming|first=Holmes|last=Chan|work=[[Hong Kong Free Press]]|date=14 July 2019|access-date=6 May 2021}}</ref>
 
In April 2021, the [[Hong Kong University Students' Union]] criticized Zhang, and said that he was promoting [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security education]] as a "political task" and was "destroying the autonomy of institutions."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hk.on.cc/hk/bkn/cnt/news/20210419/bkn-20210419114020494-0419_00822_001.html |script-title=zh:官媒指港大學生會抹黑一國兩制 成員「玩火必自焚」 |date=19 April 2021 |website=[[Oriental Daily News]] |access-date=27 May 2025 |language=zh}}</ref>

In October 2023, Zhang was accused by whistleblowers of potential misconduct, including the purchase of a HK$2 million (US$255,370) BMW vehicle without going through an open tender.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tse |first=Hans |title=University of Hong Kong's ruling body axes meeting on school head's misconduct allegations - Hong Kong Free Press HKFP |url=https://hongkongfp.com/2023/10/04/university-of-hong-kongs-ruling-body-axes-meeting-on-school-heads-misconduct-allegations/ |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=hongkongfp.com |date=4 October 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-04 |title=Exclusive: University of Hong Kong council pushes back against head over bombshell claims |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/3236808/tensions-deepen-university-hong-kong-president-slams-handling-bombshell-claims-against-him |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=South China Morning Post }}</ref>
